newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sees dollar level too high vs won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sees dollar level too high vs won.

text.p: The Bank of Korea thinks the current dollar level is too high against the won and plans intervention, a bank official said on Friday.
The central bank official, who asked not to be identified, warned that further dollar build-ups at the 880 won level would lead to losses.
"If one goes long at the 880 level, he will risk losses," the official said.
The won is trading at 879.20 in mid-morning on Friday.
"The exchange rate has risen too much in March and we are ready to intervene with the same intensity as we did in February," the official said.
Intensive central bank intervention in February reversed the won's fall and pushed its value sharply higher.
The South Korean unit strengthened by 33.5 won to 853.50 won on February 20 from 887.00 won two days earlier after falling from 864.50 at the beginning of the month.
